items.prompt: Which statement separates a diagnosis from a prediction?
options: A diagnosis identifies a condition; it does not specify one person's exact future course.
A diagnosis determines the exact age at which every symptom will occur.
A diagnosis makes follow-up observations unnecessary.
A diagnosis and a prognosis are always identical.
items.rationale: Diagnosis and prognosis answer different questions, and SCA3 trajectories vary between people.

items.prompt: What is the safest interpretation of an ATXN3 repeat result?
options: It should be interpreted with qualified clinical or genetic counselling context.
It precisely determines future annual SARA change.
It proves that a particular treatment will work.
It replaces neurological assessment.
items.rationale: A molecular result is clinically meaningful, but it is not a precise individual forecast or treatment recommendation.

items.prompt: A cohort reports a mean annual SARA increase of 1.49 points. What follows?
options: The cohort average describes that study and carries uncertainty; it is not an individual forecast.
Every participant increased by exactly 1.49 points.
Any future SCA3 cohort must have the same mean.
The estimate proves a treatment effect.
items.rationale: A mean combines varied trajectories and depends on cohort, measurement and follow-up.

items.prompt: Why report both a confidence interval and a prediction interval in a meta-analysis?
options: They address uncertainty in the pooled mean and expected variation across settings, respectively.
They are two visual styles for the same quantity.
The prediction interval predicts one patient's next score.
Only the narrower interval should be disclosed.
items.rationale: The intervals answer different population-level questions and neither is a personal prognosis.

items.prompt: What can a ClinicalTrials.gov registration establish by itself?
options: That a study was registered with stated design information, not that its intervention works.
That the intervention is effective.
That all registered outcomes were positive.
That regulators approved the intervention.
items.rationale: A registry record describes a study; results and evidentiary conclusions require separate assessment.

items.prompt: What is an appropriate conclusion from post-mortem RNA expression differences?
options: They can generate and test molecular hypotheses that require replication.
They diagnose SCA3 in a living individual.
They prove the direction of disease causality.
They identify an effective treatment without further experiments.
items.rationale: Tissue associations are scientifically useful but do not establish diagnosis, causality or efficacy.

The treatment has an 80% probability of working for a patient.
Exactly 80% of trial participants improve.
The simulated participants were observed patients.
items.rationale: Power is an operating characteristic of a design under assumptions, not an efficacy probability.

items.prompt: Why simulate MAR dropout separately from MCAR dropout?
options: Because dropout related to observed severity can change bias and retained information differently from random dropout.
Because MAR guarantees that no data are missing.
Because MCAR always creates treatment benefit.
Because the two labels are interchangeable.
items.rationale: Missingness assumptions are part of the data-generating model and should be stress-tested.

items.prompt: A biomarker changes across disease stages. What remains unresolved?
options: Whether changing the biomarker improves clinical outcomes and whether it is valid for an individual use.
Nothing; stage association proves clinical benefit.
Only the chart colour.
Whether any participants were measured.
items.rationale: Association, intervention responsiveness and individual validity are separate evidentiary questions.

items.prompt: What strengthens confidence in a molecular pathway signal?
options: Prespecified analysis, multiplicity control and replication in an independent compatible dataset.
Selecting the smallest unadjusted p-value after looking at all analyses.
Treating tissue regions from one donor as different people.
Removing results that disagree with the hypothesis.
items.rationale: Transparent analysis and independent replication reduce selective and pseudo-replication biases.

items.prompt: Which preparation best supports a focused clinical conversation?
options: A dated observation timeline plus prioritized questions and uncertainty.
An AI-generated diagnosis presented as fact.
A list that mixes observations, assumptions and treatment instructions.
Uploading family health information to an ungoverned public system.
items.rationale: Structured observations and questions support dialogue without replacing clinical judgement.

items.prompt: How should uncertainty be communicated to a family?
options: State what is known, what is uncertain, the evidence source and which question needs a professional.
Hide uncertainty to make the answer feel reassuring.
Convert a cohort average into a personal timetable.
Use technical terminology without checking understanding.
items.rationale: Calibrated communication preserves both usefulness and epistemic honesty.
